result:
Post revisions are in place. `bun run typecheck` passes and `guren check` reports no failures (5 warnings, which I didn't look into). I haven't run the app or the test suite, and I didn't add tests, so none of the new routes or behaviour has been exercised.

- **Storage:** `post_revisions` (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at` as ISO text) is added in `db/schema.ts`, with a generated migration `db/migrations/20261023005416_post_revisions`. You'll need to run `bun run db:migrate` to apply it. The model is `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`, with a `keep(post)` helper that saves a post's current title, excerpt and body as a revision.
- **Editing:** `PostController.update` now calls `PostRevision.keep(post)` after the policy check and validation pass. Refused saves and creates keep nothing. Saving an edit that changes nothing still keeps a revision.
- **Deleting:** `PostController.destroy` deletes the post's revisions before deleting the post.
- **Revisions page:** `GET /posts/:id/revisions` is handled by the new `PostRevisionController`. It passes `revisions: [{ id, title, createdAt }]`, newest first by id, plus the post's id and title. The page is `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx`, and the post page has a "History" link, shown only to the author.
- **Restore:** `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` keeps the post's current version as a new revision, then writes the chosen revision's fields back and redirects to `/posts/:id`. The restored revision stays in the list.
- **Access:**
  - Both routes sit behind the `auth` middleware, so guests go to `/login`.
  - Both use the existing `update` policy, so other signed-in users get 403.
  - A `revisionId` that belongs to a different post gets 404.
